how-to-play-wordle.title: How to play Wordle: rules, colours and repeated letters
how-to-play-wordle.seo_title: How to Play Wordle: Rules & Tile Colours
how-to-play-wordle.description: Learn how to play Wordle, including the six-guess rules, green, yellow and grey feedback, Hard Mode and repeated letters.
how-to-play-wordle.intro: Guess one five-letter word in six tries. Every submitted row returns position-by-position feedback that narrows the next guess.

sections.heading: The basic loop
paragraphs: Type a valid five-letter word and submit it. Read all five feedback tiles before choosing the next word. The puzzle ends when every tile is green or all six rows have been used.
The official game maintains its own accepted-word list. A word appearing in a general dictionary does not guarantee that the game accepts it.

sections.heading: What do Wordle colours mean?
paragraphs: Green means the letter is correct and in that exact position. Yellow means the answer contains that letter, but not in that position. Grey means the guess used no remaining copy of that letter.

example.label: Example feedback row: green S, grey T, yellow A, grey R, green E
example.explanation: This row fixes S and E, moves A elsewhere, and removes the unmatched T and R from consideration.

sections.heading: Repeated letters need careful reading
paragraphs: Feedback is allocated to exact matches first. Remaining copies are then allocated to yellow matches. If a guess contains two Es but the answer has only one, one E can be green or yellow while the other is grey.
That grey tile limits the number of copies; it does not necessarily eliminate the letter entirely.

sections.heading: Hard mode and ordinary play
paragraphs: The official game may offer optional settings such as Hard Mode. This guide explains the ordinary feedback rules and does not claim that every strategy is legal under every optional setting.

sections.heading: How does Wordle work?
paragraphs: Every guess supplies constraints for the hidden five-letter answer. Green fixes a position, yellow keeps a letter but moves it, and grey removes only the copies that were not allocated to green or yellow tiles. A careful next guess must satisfy the complete pattern rather than treating each tile in isolation.

sections.heading: Can a Wordle answer use the same letter twice?
paragraphs: Yes. Answers and guesses can contain repeated letters. The feedback may colour one copy green or yellow and another copy grey when the answer contains fewer copies than the guess.

sections.heading: What happens after six guesses?
paragraphs: The daily attempt ends after the sixth submitted row if the answer has not been found. You can still review the feedback to see which constraints were missed, but this independent guide does not host or reset the official game.

wordle-strategy.title: Wordle strategy: starting words, tips and repeated letters
wordle-strategy.description: Choose useful Wordle starting words, plan stronger second guesses, understand common-letter coverage and handle duplicate letters.
wordle-strategy.intro: Good play is less about memorising one magic opener and more about turning each row into reliable constraints.

sections.heading: How to compare the best Wordle starting words
paragraphs: A useful opener normally combines common letters with few duplicates, giving the first row several chances to reveal information. Different vocabularies and play preferences produce different sensible choices, so no starting word is guaranteed to be best.

Words such as CRANE, SLATE or TRACE illustrate broad letter coverage, but they are examples rather than a universal ranking. After the first row, the actual feedback matters more than the reputation of the opener.

sections.heading: Plan the second guess from the first result
paragraphs: A strong second guess responds to what the opener revealed. When the first row is mostly grey, testing several new letters may be useful. When it gives multiple greens or yellows, preserve those constraints and compare the smaller set of plausible patterns.
Do not repeat a known absent letter merely to reuse a familiar word unless you have a deliberate information goal and your selected game mode permits it.

sections.heading: Respect every confirmed position
items: Keep green letters fixed unless you are deliberately testing information in a mode that permits it.
Move yellow letters to untested positions instead of repeating a known failure.
Treat grey feedback as a count constraint when the same letter appears more than once.
Compare the whole feedback pattern, not one tile at a time.

sections.heading: Know when to test a duplicate
paragraphs: Early guesses often benefit from five distinct letters, but repetition becomes valuable when the pattern points toward a word family with doubled letters. The right time to test a duplicate is when it separates plausible candidates, not because repeats are generally good or bad.

sections.heading: Common letters are a guide, not a guarantee
paragraphs: Frequent letters can make an opener informative across a broad vocabulary, but daily answers can contain uncommon letters or repeated characters. Letter frequency helps compare options; it cannot identify a specific answer without feedback.
A balanced strategy therefore combines coverage with position information and the remaining candidate patterns.

sections.heading: Adjust the plan for Hard Mode
paragraphs: Hard Mode may require later guesses to reuse revealed hints. That limits pure information guesses, so check the official setting rules and choose a candidate that respects every enforced clue.

sections.heading: Use a solver as a constraint checker
paragraphs: A solver is most helpful when it preserves the feedback exactly and explains vocabulary limits. Zero results can indicate contradictory feedback, but it can also mean that the answer is outside the solver’s list.

about.title: About Wordle Hint Today
about.description: Learn what Wordle Hint Today offers, how daily puzzle information is checked and sourced, and how to report a correction.
about.intro: Wordle Hint Today is an independent help site with progressive daily clues, controlled answer reveals, a browser-based solver and links to published past puzzles.

sections.heading: What this website offers
paragraphs: The daily page starts with spoiler-free guidance and lets each reader choose whether to reveal a meaning clue, letter facts, individual letters or the complete answer. The archive links only to puzzle dates that have actually been published, and the solver filters its local word list from the feedback a reader enters.
Daily pages are generated ahead of each visit, so opening a hint does not contact the puzzle source or send solver entries to the publisher.

sections.heading: How puzzle information is checked
paragraphs: The publisher retrieves the public daily puzzle record and checks that its date, puzzle number and five-letter answer agree with the expected structure before a page can be published. The displayed letter counts and repeated-letter status are calculated from that checked answer rather than written by hand.

A gentle meaning clue appears only when the answer has a suitable non-circular definition in the locally imported Princeton WordNet data. If no suitable definition is available, the factual letter hints remain available without a fabricated clue.

sections.heading: Independent status
paragraphs: This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by The New York Times. It links to the official Wordle game and does not present itself as the game.

sections.heading: Vocabulary and definition sources
paragraphs: Solver candidates are derived from the pinned ESDB 2026.02.25 American English dictionaries. Optional meaning clues are derived from Princeton WordNet 3.0. Both datasets are filtered locally and used under their accompanying licenses.

sections.heading: Corrections
paragraphs: Send a suspected wrong date, puzzle number, answer or clue to the contact address in the site footer and include the affected page URL. Confirmed corrections retain the earlier record internally and can display a correction notice on the updated page.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: Privacy information for Wordle Hint Today, including local browser processing and hosting logs.
privacy.intro: The site stores no visitor account and sends no solver guesses to the publisher.

sections.heading: Local date and solver data
paragraphs: The browser reads its resolved timezone and local calendar date to show the matching published hints on the homepage. It does not request location permission or use IP geolocation.
Solver guesses and feedback remain in the current page session and are not persisted across visits in the initial release.

sections.heading: Storage on your device
paragraphs: The initial release does not use cookies or local storage for guesses, spoiler state or a remembered date override. Normal browser cache behavior may retain static files.

sections.heading: Hosting and monitoring
paragraphs: The static site is hosted by Hostinger. Hostinger and its CDN may process IP addresses, request paths, browser identifiers and timestamps in technical security and access logs under their policies. This site does not currently add advertising, account tracking or analytics scripts.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: Privacy and correction requests can be sent to the contact address displayed in the site footer.
